title_en: Greetings & Introductions — speak on day one
subtitle: Meet someone, say your name, leave politely
description: The ten phrases that open every Chinese conversation: hello, how are you, your name, nice to meet you, thanks and goodbye — English + ខ្មែរ support, native Mandarin audio on every line.

spine.title: The route · one first meeting
spine.note: Greet → ask the name → answer about yourself → say nice to meet you → part politely. One conversation, in order.

explain.title: The big picture
explain.why: A first meeting in Chinese is a fixed little dance of five moves. Learn one line per move and you can hold the whole conversation — no grammar needed yet.

tiles.en: One hello fits almost every situation
Add 心 at the bottom = respect
Bye, or the friendlier 'see you tomorrow'
One word offers, invites and softens

cards.alt: Two flat figures facing each other with a speech bubble
cards.ko: 你好！Nǐ hǎo — 最常用的打招呼。
cards.en: Hello! Works with almost anyone, anywhere.
cards.km: សួស្តី! ប្រើបានជិតគ្រប់កន្លែង។

cards.alt: A figure with a heart under the character 您
cards.ko: 对长辈、客户说：您好！Nín hǎo。
cards.en: Say 您好 (nín hǎo) to elders, teachers and customers — it carries respect.
cards.km: ចំពោះ មនុស្សចាស់ គ្រូ ឬ អតិថិជន៖ ជម្រាបសួរ។

cards.alt: A speech bubble with an upward arrow and a heart
cards.ko: 你好吗？Nǐ hǎo ma — 问别人怎么样。
cards.en: How are you? A real question, but friends often skip it.
cards.km: តើ អ្នក សុខសប្បាយ ទេ?

cards.alt: A name tag with the character 叫
cards.ko: 我叫 + 名字：我叫 Dara。
cards.en: 'My name is …' — literally 'I am-called Dara'. Put your name right after 叫.
cards.km: ខ្ញុំ ឈ្មោះ តារា។

cards.alt: A question bubble with a name tag inside
cards.ko: 请问，你叫什么名字？Qǐng wèn…
cards.en: 'May I ask your name?' — start with 请问 to sound polite.
cards.km: សុំ ទោស តើ អ្នក ឈ្មោះ អ្វី?

cards.alt: A thumbs-up over a smiley face
cards.ko: 我很好，谢谢。Wǒ hěn hǎo, xiè xie.
cards.en: I'm very well, thank you — the standard bright answer.
cards.km: ខ្ញុំ សុខសប្បាយ អរគុណ។

cards.alt: Two hands meeting over a small heart
cards.ko: 很高兴认识你！Hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
cards.en: Nice to meet you! Say it right after names are exchanged.
cards.km: រីករាយ ដែល បាន ស្គាល់ គ្នា!

cards.ko: 再见！Zàijiàn — 或者更自然：明天见！
cards.en: Goodbye! Even more natural with people you'll see again: 'See you tomorrow'.
cards.km: លា ហើយ! ឬ៖ ជួប គ្នា សែក!

cards.alt: A teapot pouring a cup with the character 请
cards.ko: 请坐，请喝茶，请先走 — 一个“请”走遍中国。
cards.en: Please sit, please have tea, after you — one 请 softens everything.
cards.km: សូម អង្គុយ សូម ផឹក តែ សូម ទៅ មុន។

cards.alt: Two pressed hands over a heart for thank you
cards.ko: 别人帮你：谢谢！他说：不客气。
cards.en: Someone helps: xiè xie (thank you). The reply is 不客气 — 'you're welcome'.
cards.km: អរគុណ! ចម្លើយ៖ មិន អី ទេ។

qa_note: Recall the answer in your head first, then tap to check and listen.

items.qen: When do I use the polite 您?
items.a: 长辈、老师、客户、第一次见的客人。朋友用你。
items.aen: Elders, teachers, customers, guests you just met. With friends, plain 你.
items.akm: មនុស្សចាស់ គ្រូ អតិថិជន។ ជាមួយ មិត្ត ប្រើ nǐ។
items.why: One syllable buys you real goodwill. When unsure, 您 is the safer mistake.

items.qen: Is 'Have you eaten?' an invitation to dinner?
items.a: 不是，那只是打招呼。回答：吃了，你呢？
items.aen: No — it's just a greeting among friends. Answer: 吃了，你呢? (Yes, and you?)
items.akm: មិន មែន ទេ — នេះ គ្រាន់ តែ សំណូម ពរ ប៉ុណ្ណោះ។ ឆ្លើយ៖ បរិភោគ រួច ហើយ។

items.qen: What do I say first on a phone call?
items.a: 电话里说“喂”（wéi），然后说自己是谁。
items.aen: On the phone Chinese says 喂 (wéi), then your own name — not 你好.
items.akm: ពេល ទូរស័ព្ទ គេ និយាយ wéi ហើយ ប្រាប់ ឈ្មោះ ខ្លួន។
items.why: Textbooks teach 你好; real phones start with wéi. Knowing this instantly sounds natural.

qa.title: Real conversations
qa.small: What someone will actually ask you

items.aen: My name is Dara. And you?
items.akm: ខ្ញុំ ឈ្មោះ តារា។ អ្នកវិញ?

items.aen: He's my friend. His name is Sok.
items.akm: គាត់ ជា មិត្ត ខ្ញុំ ឈ្មោះ សុខ។

items.qen: Nice to meet you. (they say it first)
items.aen: I'm also very glad to meet you.
items.akm: ខ្ញុំ ក៏ រីករាយ ដែល បាន ស្គាល់ គ្នា ដែរ។

items.km: តើ អ្នក និយាយ ភាសា អង់គ្លេស ទេ?
សូម និយាយ ម្តង ទៀត។

items.en: I have to go now — goodbye!
items.km: ខ្ញុំ ត្រូវ ទៅ ហើយ លា ហើយ!

qa.title: Patterns · sound Chinese from day one

items.qen: Pattern: 我叫 + name — 'I am called …'
items.aen: He's called Sok. She's called Malis.
items.akm: គាត់ ឈ្មោះ សុខ។ នាង ឈ្មោះ មាលីស។

items.qen: Pattern: 我是 + thing — 'I am a …' (no verb change)
items.aen: He is a teacher. We are friends. 是 never conjugates.
items.akm: គាត់ ជា គ្រូ។ យើង ជា មិត្ត។

items.qen: Pattern: X 呢? = 'And X?' — the fastest way to bounce a question back.
items.aen: I'm well — and you? — I'm well too.
items.akm: ខ្ញុំ សុខសប្បាយ អ្នកវិញ? — ខ្ញុំ ក៏ ដូចគ្នា។

items.km: អរុណ សួស្តី
រាត្រី សួស្តី
ជួប គ្នា សែក
ท่าน / អ្នក (គោរព)
មិត្តភក្តិ
មិន អី ទេ
មិន ជា បាប ទេ

full.title: 见面 · Saying hello
full.ko: 你好！Nǐ hǎo — 最常用的打招呼。 对长辈、客户说：您好！Nín hǎo。 你好吗？Nǐ hǎo ma — 问别人怎么样。
full.en: Hello! Works with almost anyone, anywhere. Say 您好 (nín hǎo) to elders, teachers and customers — it carries respect. How are you? A real question, but friends often skip it.

full.title: 名字 · Names
full.ko: 我叫 + 名字：我叫 Dara。 请问，你叫什么名字？Qǐng wèn…
full.en: 'My name is …' — literally 'I am-called Dara'. Put your name right after 叫. 'May I ask your name?' — start with 请问 to sound polite.

full.title: 回答 · Answering
full.ko: 我很好，谢谢。Wǒ hěn hǎo, xiè xie. 很高兴认识你！Hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
full.en: I'm very well, thank you — the standard bright answer. Nice to meet you! Say it right after names are exchanged.

full.title: 再见 · Saying goodbye
full.ko: 再见！Zàijiàn — 或者更自然：明天见！
full.en: Goodbye! Even more natural with people you'll see again: 'See you tomorrow'.

full.title: 礼貌 · Being polite
full.ko: 请坐，请喝茶，请先走 — 一个“请”走遍中国。 别人帮你：谢谢！他说：不客气。
full.en: Please sit, please have tea, after you — one 请 softens everything. Someone helps: xiè xie (thank you). The reply is 不客气 — 'you're welcome'.
